title: TileData Custom Data UI Values are incorrectly painted from any Collections (Arrays or Dict)
body: ### Tested versions - Godot Stable 4.6.3 and DEV 4.7 (Latest as of 1st June) ### System information Windows 10. This bug is not hardwared related, the issue is present in any OS and Hardwared it is Godot Source Logic issue ### Issue description Short explanation: When picking a CustomData value to add it to a TileData within a TileSet, we have these problems 1. In some scenarios, the Godot Custom Data in the "UI" does not represent and does not sync with the value that is painted. 2. Adding/Removing Members to a Collection does not refresh the UI until we click and "toggle" the header. Clicking on the Header "PackedVector2Array" is needed to refresh the screen, but it should automatically happen when adding/removing members. DETAILED EXPLANATION AND ROOT CAUSE ANALYSES. 0. The TileSet Paint editor stores the current value we are about to paint in a DummyObject. For example: DummyObject::properties["custom_data_2"] When the collection UI emits a new value, TileDataDefaultEditor::_property_value_changed() writes that value into the dummy object: dummy_object->set(p_property, p_value); The Original code is basically: ``` void TileDataDefaultEditor::_property_value_changed(const StringName &p_property, const Variant &p_value, const StringName &p_field) { ERR_FAIL_NULL(dummy_object); dummy_object->set(p_property, p_value); emit_signal(SNAME("needs_redraw")); } ``` 1. It seems that in Godot, collection editors have their own internal storage. For arrays and PackedArrays, this is EditorPropertyArrayObject::array. For dictionaries, this is EditorPropertyDictionaryObject::dict. What I understand reading the code is that Godot needs this internal storage because collection editors are made of child editors: element 0, element 1, key/value rows, size controls, add/remove buttons, etc. Scalar editors do not need the same kind of internal collection proxy. 2. Before any fix, TileDataDefaultEditor update the DummyObject but does not ask the collection editor to refresh itself. That meant the DummyObject could contain the correct current paint value, while EditorPropertyArrayObject::array or EditorPropertyDictionaryObject::dict still contained an older value. The visible UI rows could also show stale values, or fail to show/hide rows after resizing. 3. The fix I would like to propose is a small a very small surgical change, and in my testing it works so far. After writing the emitted value into the DummyObject, TileDataDefaultEditor should check whether the hosted editor is an EditorPropertyArray or EditorPropertyDictionary. If it is, it calls update_property() so the collection editor refreshes from the DummyObject. ``` void TileDataDefaultEditor::_property_value_changed(const StringName &p_property, const Variant &p_value, const StringName &p_field) { ERR_FAIL_NULL(dummy_object); dummy_object->set(p_property, p_value); if (property_editor && (Object::cast_to(property_editor) || Object::cast_to(property_editor))) { property_editor->update_property(); } emit_signal(SNAME("needs_redraw")); } ``` This keeps the collection editor UI and its internal storage in sync with the paint value. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a TileSet Resource 2. Create a Custom Data that is a Collection (Array, Dictonary, etc) 3. Go and try to Paint the Custom Data in the "Paint Properties" of the TileSet Editor. 4. Try and resize the Array and Dictonary (UI should not show the new member slots) 5. Add new items and toggle the UI refresh forcing it by clicking on the "Header" -> It should display the values. 6. Change the values and paint + Change it again and paint, it should not paing the correct values. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Added a MRP, but to get it to see the issue, you need to follow the steps to reproduce. As it needs an update and changes to the Collection Values and painting.
